analyzed_vuln.description: EvaluateExpression compiles an initializer using a temporary runtime stack, but its post-compilation stack-capacity check relies on o->maxStackSlots. Slot allocation updates that field through TouchSlot only when o->function is non-NULL; expression compilation deliberately has o->function == NULL, so maxStackSlots remains zero even when emitted Const64 operations target slots beyond the runtime stack. The ineffective ValidateBlockEnd logic also accepts an initializer with surplus stack values, allowing attacker-controlled sequences of constants to consume progressively higher slots. RunCode then executes the generated code and op_Const64 writes 8 bytes through the unchecked emitted slot offset, causing the heap-buffer-overflow.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Supply a parseable Wasm module containing an active data segment whose init expression consists of enough permitted constant opcodes (notably i64.const values) before end to allocate a destination slot beyond the runtime stack. ParseSection_Data stores the expression, m3_LoadModule calls InitDataSegments, and EvaluateExpression compiles it with o->function == NULL. In this harness m3_NewRuntime provides only a 128-byte Wasm stack (plus a small allocation cushion); the malformed expression's surplus values are not rejected and its true slot high-water mark is not recorded, so the maxStackSlots-versus-numStackSlots check passes and executing an emitted Const64 performs the out-of-bounds write.

args: In wasm3/source/m3_compile.c, what is the correct intended validation at ValidateBlockEnd(), especially for initializer expressions compiled via EvaluateExpression in wasm3/source/m3_env.c? Should it require GetNumBlockValuesOnStack(o) to exactly equal block result count and validate each result type? Also, is making TouchSlot update maxStackSlots even when o->function is NULL safe and sufficient for expression compilation?

The reported heap overflow occurs because EvaluateExpression compiles malformed data-segment initializer expressions with many i64.const operations. CompileBlock accepts surplus values because ValidateBlockEnd is stubbed. Slot allocation calls TouchSlot, but TouchSlot only updates maxStackSlots when o->function is non-NULL; EvaluateExpression deliberately leaves function NULL. EvaluateExpression then compares maxStackSlots with runtime.numStackSlots, sees zero, and RunCode executes op_Const64 at an out-of-bounds slot. I am considering two complementary root fixes: unconditionally tracking maxStackSlots in TouchSlot, while retaining the comment that function entry consumes it only for functions; and implementing exact block-end stack arity/type validation. I need to preserve polymorphic/unreachable block behavior and multi-value semantics.
